display.purpose: Page titles and landing headlines. Space Grotesk, mechanical without novelty.

body.purpose: Prose, form values, list content. Inter, invisible by design.

label.purpose: Mono uppercase micro-label at 0.07em. Field labels, stat captions, table headers, section markers — the system's most repeated gesture.

readout.purpose: Money, counts, durations, IDs, timestamps. Always tabular so columns align.

shadows.name: chassis-mount
shadows.purpose: The sidebar rail only. The inset highlight is the top bevel of a mounted panel.

shadows.name: bench-tight
shadows.purpose: Objects resting on the bench — the repair ticket, the product frame. Short throw, close contact.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Hover response of an interactive card, paired with translateY(-2px). Never a resting state.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Modals, sheets, the featured plan plate. Genuinely floating above everything.

shadows.name: powered
shadows.purpose: The only colored shadow in the system. Under primary buttons and brand-active elements; means energized, not important.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Focus state on inputs and icon buttons, alongside a border shift to brand.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default easing. Mechanical departure, soft arrival.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: Symmetric transitions such as pulsing LEDs.

motion.name: ease-emphasized
motion.purpose: Entrances that need a longer settle.

motion.name: dur-fast
motion.purpose: Control state changes: hover, focus, press.

motion.name: dur-normal
motion.purpose: Surface changes: card lift, theme swap, route fade.

notes: Dual theme: frontmatter carries the dark theme (default). Light theme re-binds the same token names in src/styles/tokens.css.
The readout-* family is defined once and never re-bound per theme, which is what makes an instrument well look identical in dark and light.
Breakpoints that decide fits/does-not-fit must be @container, not @media — app zoom adds layout space without moving media queries.

narrative.overview:
The interface is a technician's bench, not a dashboard. Every surface behaves like a piece of shop equipment: a graphite chassis with things mounted on it, instruments that read out in monospace, status carried by lit indicators rather than by words, and seams that look machined rather than drawn. The operator is standing at a counter with a customer waiting and a device in one hand — so the system favors the glance over the read, and the exact number over the friendly approximation.

Three pillars carry the whole palette. Graphite steel is the neutral ground: cool, slightly blue, never warm grey and never office-paper white. Safety amber (#f5a623) is the single brand voice — the color of a machine that is powered and doing something. Diagnostic cyan (#3dd9c4) is the instrument voice — measurement, liveness, information that the machine reports about itself.

Both themes are first class and neither is a tint of the other. Dark is "Graphite Workshop"; light is "Bright Workshop Steel" — cool anodized metal, deliberately not a bright paper document. A component is finished only when it has been judged in both. The confirmed anti-reference is generic SaaS: stock component-library chrome, a padlock glyph for a gated feature, a soft rounded card with a pastel icon standing in for content.
keyCharacteristics: Monospace for every number, ID, code, and status readout — the single strongest signal that this is instrumentation
Status is a lit LED plus a value, never a word alone
Colored spine on the leading edge of cards and rows, not a full colored surface
Dotted and perforated seams instead of solid rules
Machined radii (5/8/12/16/24px) — never fully rounded except for pills and indicators
Two themes at equal weight, guaranteed by tokens rather than by review

rules.name: The Token-Only Rule
rules.body: No hex, rgb(), or hsl() literal ever appears in feature CSS. Every color resolves through var(--token) from src/styles/tokens.css. This is not a style preference — it is the mechanism that guarantees both themes are correct without anyone checking. The one sanctioned exception is the readout family, which is already theme-independent by design.

rules.name: The One Amber Rule
rules.body: Safety amber marks the single most important action or the single active state in a view. Two ambers competing on one screen means neither is the answer. Cyan is not a second brand color to reach for when amber feels repetitive — it means instrument reading, and using it decoratively drains it.

rules.name: The Lit-Signal Rule
rules.body: A status is an LED plus a value, never a word alone and never a color alone. The LED is 7–9px, filled with the signal color, and carries a matching box-shadow glow at 6–9px blur. A colorblind operator reads the value; a glancing operator reads the light.

rules.name: The Mono Numbers Rule
rules.body: Every number a user might compare, verify, or read aloud is monospace with tabular figures: currency, quantities, service IDs (FM-0241), phone numbers, times, percentages. Proportional digits in an operational readout is a defect, not a preference.

rules.name: The 12px Floor Rule
rules.body: No leaf text that carries information or an action goes below 12px at the default 16px root. Non-interactive ornament may be smaller. This is an ergonomic contract, not a suggestion — the operator is reading at arm's length under shop lighting.

rules.name: The Container Query Rule
rules.body: Any breakpoint that decides fits / does not fit — table versus cards, one column versus two — must be a @container query, never @media. Two measured reasons: the app's own zoom control adds layout space without moving media queries (em units do not help; they resolve against the initial font size), and the sidebar appears at ≥1025px so content space shrinks as the viewport widens, producing a broken band no single max-width can express. Derive the threshold from measured min-content, not a round number.

rules.name: The Zoom-Aware Viewport Rule
rules.body: Any element sized to the screen uses --app-vh, never bare 100vh/100dvh. The CSS zoom property scales viewport units, so a raw 100dvh shell leaves dead space below 100% zoom and overflows above it.

rules.name: The Mounted-or-Flat Rule
rules.body: A surface earns a shadow by being mounted chassis (rail, topbar), a true overlay (modal, toast, dropdown, bottom sheet), or an object resting on the bench (ticket, frame). Everything else is flat at rest and may acquire --shadow-md only as a hover response. A resting content card with a drop shadow is drift.

rules.name: The Ambient Bench Rule
rules.body: The blueprint grid and its two radial washes on body::before are the system's only ambient depth. Individual sections do not get their own decorative glow; they get a tonal step or a border.

rules.name: The Spine, Not the Fill Rule
rules.body: Category and status are carried by the 3px leading spine, never by flooding a card or row with a tinted background. A border-left heavier than 3px, or a colored surface standing in for the spine, is a different system.

rules.name: The Earned Well Rule
rules.body: The instrument well is not a surface anyone may reach for. It is earned by content that is genuinely an instrument reading — a live operational value the operator checks at a glance (net profit, the flow of a job through states, the plan that is the recommended answer) — and it is budgeted at one per viewport. A long scrolling page may carry one per chapter, provided two are never in view together. Its power is scarcity: a screen showing three wells has none. When a panel merely needs to feel important, it gets a tonal step and a border instead.

dos: Do resolve every color through var(--token) from src/styles/tokens.css, and judge every new component in both themes before calling it done.
Do set numbers in JetBrains Mono with tabular figures — money, counts, IDs, times, percentages.
Do pair a signal color with a lit LED and a readable value, so status survives both a glance and colorblindness.
Do classify cards and rows with the 3px diagnostic spine.
Do use 1px dotted seams for internal division instead of solid rules.
Do use @container for any breakpoint that decides whether content fits, and derive the threshold from measured min-content.
Do keep informational leaf text at 12px or above and interactive targets at 44×44px on touch.
Do give a gated feature a dimmed channel and a mono "PRO" badge with a brand LED.
donts: Don't hardcode a hex, rgb(), or hsl() value in feature CSS.

Don't use a padlock glyph, or any stock component-library chrome, to mark a plan-gated feature — that gets the dimmed channel and the mono "PRO" badge. A lock icon on a genuine permission denial is a different message and stays.
Don't put a drop shadow on a content surface at rest — shadow means mounted, overlaid, or just-lifted.
Don't widen the colored spine past 3px or replace it with a flooded background tint.
Don't place more than one instrument well on a screen, or use the readout palette for a panel that merely wants attention.
Don't reach for diagnostic cyan as a second brand color when amber starts to feel repetitive — cyan means instrument reading.
Don't put white text on safety amber; amber always carries --on-brand (#1a1205).

Don't apply glass or backdrop-filter to a card sitting in a list or grid on a page that already has its own surface. Glass belongs to things that float over something: chassis (topbar, drawers, sheets, action bars, the demo faceplate), overlays, and standalone panels resting directly on the ambient grid (auth, onboarding wizard, tracking result, the summary rail).
Don't set an operational number in a proportional face.
Don't use emoji or a Unicode glyph where an icon belongs — icons come only through the Icon component.
